I re-ordered because I thought it was a 1 time issue however I am having the same issue now for the second time. Basically with both items on the second day of use they began to get a weird bubbling as shown in the photos and then proceeded to fog up in the showe after that. The installation was a breeze and the adhesive works flawlessly, unfortunately. thats the only thing. The mirror fogged up in less than three days of use. reviews.t: Best adhesive ever; worst mirror ever.
reviews.x: I've had this hanging in my shower for nearly two years now, and I am *completely* sold on the adhesive. My shower wall is square tiles, and this overhangs one tile by an inch or two on each side.  But it doesn't seem to matter, because it just sticks and stays there.  Unlike suction-cup systems, this has NEVER fallen. It hasn't become brittle. It isn't nearly as limited in the places you can find to get it to stick.  In short, it is perfect!!  Except for the mirror itself. The mirror is a very

reviews.t: Cool, modern mirror but terrible anti-fog
reviews.x: Attached is a picture of the mirror just after I started up the shower. The water was barely warm at this point, and it was already completely fogged up.  The mirror itself looks cool and modern. It's on the small side, and adheres well to the shower door. However, the image in the mirror is distorted, sort of like a toned down version of those mirrors you see at a carnival or a state fair. It's still usable for shaving purposes, but the fog is a real issue.  Will likely return this and look for
The mirror really sticks well to smooth surfaces, but has no anti-fog abilities. It fogs up instantly to the point of no use. Will be returning this one.

The product itself isn't that bad to be honest, but this listing is full of lies! How does Amazon allow them to get away with this?  - First off, the main image on this listing has been stretch out to make it look rectangular (I know the product is at an angle, it has still been stretched out). - The listed dimensions are also misleading (borderline dishonest in my opinion) as the height includes the length of the pointless tab on the bottom. The ACTUAL mirror dimensions are a 5.125" square. - T

I saw a lot of people complaining that this doesn't stay put, won't stick to a surface that's not completely flat, and can't be remounted if it's taken down. I tested each of these theories and, as you can see in my pic, it stays put even though it's on a ridge.  If you remove or move it you just need to make sure of s few things. When putting it back up, make sure the back of it and the new surface are completely dry. Put it up with nothing in or on it. Leave it in place for a few minutes befor

reviews.t: It was greate while the anti-fog film lasted
reviews.x: It worked great, for about 4 months, then the anti-fog film pealed in the corner and it was 1 month before it was all gone and looks terrible. Can still work, but not worth it.

reviews.t: One of the better shower mirrors out there
reviews.x: For some reason, it's 2019 and none of earth's greatest minds have been able to figure out how to make a shower mirror that doesn't fog up. That being said, this one comes pretty close. It is more fog resistant than your average mirror. It also sticks very well. The toothbrush/razor holder that it pairs with also works great. The only negative I have is that after some time, it developed a white kind of paste or something around the edges which is hard to clean. I've tried washing but it seems t

reviews.t: Great mirror for the price, but the "anti-fog" properties are a joke
reviews.x: The adhesive part is better than any other shower mirror I have seen or used. It sticks perfectly when you want it to but can be removed in 2 seconds without leaving anything to clean up. I wish I had this when I still lived in apartments, I would have saved some money on security deposits from more destructive adhesive methods. The "mirror" itself is pretty cheap - basically a mirror film on a waterproof cardboard-like material - but it does the job and I have not had any issues with bubbling l
works great with the mighty toothbrush holder!
I like how the mirror sticks to the shower wall, but it fogs INSTANTLY. I threw it away after 3 weeks because I was so frustrated with how terribly quick it fogs.

reviews.t: Expensive for a small mirror, BUT is exactly what we need.
reviews.x: This is the second one of these we've purchased. The first lasted a year or two and then got scratched likely by cleaning or something (unsure) but then it lost its fogproof-ness so I ordered a new to update it. The new one seems like they may have changed it slightly. Its still as easy to install and still adheres to the wall just as well. But the mirror surface has a slight texture after removing the protective film. So the reflection is ever so slightly warped but works perfectly fine. Still

The mirror is NOT Anti-fog. They give you some bullshit answer about how science is the solution. The idea is to run hit water on the mirror for 10 seconds to eliminate condensation.  The stupidity of that, is that we are smart enough to do that with any damn mirror. If you're someone who likes hot showers, like me, you'll notice the mirror fogs up again almost immediately. Their "science" is incomplete as there's a short time in which this actually works.  The pro is that it's a rubber or plast

It's quite remarkable how the mirror so easily sticks to the wall and stays. Unfortunately, the "anti-fog" feature didn't last for more than a week. However, this is easily fixed by splashing some water on the mirror and a bit of toothpaste or anti fog paste would also fix the problem quickly. I would buy this product again, but do so knowing that it's going to be "college student" level quality.
I feel like I get dizzy or a headache looking in the mirror.  It is like a fun house mirror to my old eyes.  I will give it a few more days and see if I can adjust, if not, back to Amazon it will go.

reviews.t: Perfect for tight space on marble subway tile in bathroom (not in shower)
reviews.x: I did not purchase this on Amazon, but purchased at a local store because I wanted to physically view it first.  I have a bathroom with a sink under a large window.  There is a small space between the sink and windowsill that is tiled in polished marble subway tile (with almost no grout lines).  This is my children's bathroom and I wanted to give them a mirror to help them with brushing their teeth.  I needed something small that did not require nailing or gluing and that would not break and hur

reviews.t: The mirror’s surface is damaged by the glue-backed label pasted to it!!
reviews.x: This is my second purchase of one of these mirrors.  I like to shave in the shower so the concept of a mirror which I can stick anywhere in shower stall is appealing to me. I ruined my first mirror when I used a standard glass cleaner on it, so my bad. Well I ordered a replacement and it arrived today...great!! What’s not great is that they place a sticky label right across the front of the mirror which does not peel off easily at all, and my attempt to get the sticky pieces off the mirror ended

reviews.t: Adheres well to file and fog is easily dealt with
reviews.x: It's adhered to the tiles in my shower for months, and that's exactly what I wanted. It's easy to adjust so long as you are moving it when the tiles are dry. It's obviously not a genuine mirror as a heavy glass mirror would not work. I run a hot shower and I don't see the mirror getting foggy with any consistency. When it does, I find that I can swipe it with my hand and it's fine. I use a squeegee on my shower tile when I'm done and this has a low-enough profile that I can just lightly graze it

I love this brand and their silicone adhesive line of shower items have been game changing in our house. We absolutely love them. We have the face scrubbers, razor holders, and the beer can holder (which we use for our toothpaste and 2 electric brushes).  But this mirror is horrible.. I’m so so disappointed. I tried applying and reapplying it to see if there was a pressure distorting the reflection so much- but the image is so distorted in the mirror that it makes me dizzy just to look at. The s

reviews.t: DO NOT BUY!  YOU WONT BE ABLE TO REMOVE THIS FROM YOUR SHOWER TILES!!!
reviews.x: I purchased this and after about 3 months the anti-fog properties wore off.  I struggled to use it for about 9 more months until I finally got fed up with this and stopped using it.  I attempted to take this off my shower wall today and it's been a complete disaster.  This DOES NOT easily remove from your walls.  It's all broken into small pieces on my wall and there is small bits of silicone stuck that I can't remove.  I wish I never bought this product, I absolutely hate it.

UPDATE - keeping the mirror clean an fog free has proved to be difficult. Knocking back a star. Seems like it sticks up quite brilliantly.  Hope it stays.  The plastic mirror exposed is more like 5.25"x5.1" in size.  Fogged up first time I used, but was clear after splashing water on it and keeping it wet.  Besides the fogging issue, I wish it were bigger in size.  Otherwise good little stick on shower mirror.

This product is pretty straight forward its a sticky mirror. it does pretty much that. not sure if I miss read the directions or not but definitely get the back wet before your try to stick it to your shower wall. it does stick to tile even if uneven. my only thing is they say it is anti fog and it is for like a week and then something happens and it just isn't anymore and I have no idea why.

reviews.t: You get what you pay for.
reviews.x: It does self stick, and doesn't fall down. Because of the materials it's made of, the mirror view itself is rather distorted and it does fog up. You have to wipe it down a few times per shower. For the price, it is something I can still use to apply my facial mask in the shower; but had I known of these issues beforehand, I probably would have paid more for a higher quality item.

Do yourself a favor and review their website for surfaces these work / don’t work on. I looked after I bought it, only to see their list of acceptable surfaces is shorter than unacceptable. So while the aesthetics are really cool, these do not work as well as I hoped on my tiles. I might have to resort to those 3m strips to keep things in place. 😐

claims.text: Many reviewers report the mirror fogs up quickly or instantly, making the anti-fog claim disappointing.
Reviewers widely praise the adhesive, saying it sticks strongly and stays put on various surfaces.
Some reviewers note the anti-fog coating or film degrades or peels over time, losing effectiveness.
Several reviewers find the listing or description misleading regarding the anti-fog feature.
A few reviewers mention the mirror is small or expensive for its size.

qa.q: Will it stick to my shiny tile or glass shower wall?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: Does the mirror fog up in the shower?
qa.answer: Yes, reviews report the mirror fogs up in the shower, though some say it is more fog-resistant than average [1][3][4][5][6][2].

claims.text: The mirror fogs up instantly and has no anti-fog abilities [1][3].
It is only partially anti-fog and requires wiping or wetting to stay clear [4][5].
One review says it is more fog-resistant than your average mirror [2].

qa.q: How do I attach it without suction cups or adhesive?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: Is the mirror actually shatterproof if it falls?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: Does it leave residue or damage the surface when removed?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on removal: one reports it does not easily remove and leaves silicone bits stuck to shower tiles [4], while another says removal is fine if you ensure the back and new surface are clean before remounting [1]. One review also reports a glue-backed label damaging the mirror's surface [2].

claims.text: It does not easily remove from walls and leaves small bits of silicone stuck that can't be removed [4].
Removal is fine as long as you make sure the back and new surface are clean before remounting [1].
A glue-backed label damaged the mirror's surface [2].
